zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開篇固定收益主論

油價大幅下挫，部分扭轉上週五由通膨疑慮引發的賣壓，美國公債於8月3日反彈，但長天期債券近期所受損失遠未修復。2年期殖利率下降5.4個基點至4.238%，5年期下降6.2個基點至4.388%，10年期下降5.8個基點至4.678%，30年期則回落4.5個基點至5.229%。長債殖利率一週仍上升9.1個基點、一個月上升24.3個基點，顯示市場對聯準會公信力、財政借款與通膨持續性的疑慮依然存在。

週一行情的直接催化因素，是荷莫茲海峽周邊重啟外交斡旋的可能性。美國總統川普取消原定對伊朗發動的攻擊，並表示談判將以全面重開航道為目標；伊朗則稱，與阿曼就增加船舶通行所進行的另一場磋商已有進展。布蘭特原油下跌6.95%至每桶$83.86，WTI下跌5.14%至$80.32。油價回落降低能源衝擊迫使貨幣政策提早回應的風險，買盤因而重返名目美債與抗通膨債券。

這波反彈同時反映實質利率下降與通膨補償減少，並非單純由成長疑慮驅動。10年期實質殖利率下降3.5個基點至2.415%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2.3個基點至2.263%。股債同步上漲，標普500指數上升1.48%，那斯達克100指數上升1.78%；投資人把能源價格下降視為通膨與企業利潤率壓力獲得紓解，而非需求崩跌的警訊。

不過，當日資訊仍使聯準會有理由保持審慎。美國供應管理協會（ISM）7月製造業指數升至55.6，創2022年5月以來最高，需求維持穩健、生產激增，製造商也增聘人手。紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams表示，目前利率水準適當，因為他預期通膨將在下半年下降；但保持耐心的前提，是核心通膨須建立一條可在2028年前持續回到2%的路徑。工廠活動增強而油價下降，使9月決策取決於通膨降溫能否擴及能源以外的領域。

財政融資則構成另一項抑制債市漲勢的因素。由於預估淨現金流下降，美國財政部把本季借款預估由$6,710億上調至$7,390億，並維持9月底現金餘額$9,500億的目標。交易商大致仍預期週三季度再融資公告將維持附息債標售規模不變，但融資需求增加、對國庫券的依賴上升，使長期問題更加突出：財政部何時必須承認有必要擴大附息債供給。

## 油價回落扭轉當日通膨衝擊

原油跌幅足以改變週一美債整條殖利率曲線的方向。布蘭特原油7月漲幅超過20%，上週五收在$90以上，當日油價上漲同時推升實質殖利率與通膨補償。到了週一紐約收盤，布蘭特原油下跌近7%，WTI跌逾5%；美國取消原定攻擊，降低波斯灣產油或航運再次中斷的即時機率。

各方對外交進展的說法並不完全一致。川普表示，美國與伊朗即將展開談判，重開荷莫茲海峽是較廣泛進程的第一階段，後續還將納入核議題。德黑蘭否認正與華盛頓直接談判，但伊朗外交部長Abbas Araghchi表示，與阿曼就海峽通行路線進行的磋商已進入最後階段。未參與6月較早一項安排的以色列，則在等待這項倡議能否形成可執行的協議。

即使週一下跌，上述不確定性仍使原油價格遠高於7月初水準。WTI一個月漲幅仍為16.93%，布蘭特原油則為16.80%。五個月的衝突期間，海峽航運屢受干擾；先前美伊停火協議破裂，7月底才再次嘗試暫停衝突。因此，週一行情反映的是近期中斷風險下降，而非和解已完成或能源市場已回到戰前狀態。

美債殖利率曲線也呈現這項差異。2年期與10年期利差僅收窄0.4個基點至44個基點，2年期與30年期利差則擴大0.9個基點至99.1個基點。中期債殖利率降幅略大於長端，顯示政策與通膨疑慮有所緩解，卻未消除30年期殖利率仍高於5.2%所反映的期限溢價。此前一週，2年期與30年期利差已陡峭化17.6個基點。

長天期債券的表現同樣只算部分修復。ICE美國政府債券20年以上指數週一上漲0.39%，但一週仍下跌1.46%、一個月下跌3.56%。7至10年期指數當日上漲0.23%，一個月仍下跌1.04%。能源成本下降再度為債券價格帶來一些支撐，但實質折現率累計升幅，以及市場針對長期政策與供給不確定性要求的溢價，均未因此逆轉。

美債交易活動遠低於上週五月底調整時的水準。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$1.106兆，較前一個交易日下降42.4%，共計379,162筆交易。名目附息債交易量下降43.7%至$8,546億，TIPS交易量下降71.4%至$347億；超過7年至10年期附息債的成交量下降48.8%至$1,429億。交易量減少無法判斷投資人的買賣方向，但顯示這次反彈所伴隨的部位調整，遠少於上週五的賣壓。

風險資產也證實油價下降是跨市場的主要驅動因素。標普500指數收於7,600.50點，已接近歷史高點；那斯達克100指數漲幅高於大盤。費城半導體指數上漲1.05%，但一個月仍下跌9.47%，VIX則小幅降至15.86。即使眼前能源風險下降，黃金期貨仍上漲1.45%至$4,107.80；美元指數在此前一週下跌1.47%後，週一上漲0.22%。

## Williams界定聯準會保持耐心的條件

Williams釋出的政策訊號，比7月會議上主張升息的三位異議官員更具耐心。他表示，目前3.5%至3.75%的目標區間適合支持通膨降溫，並預測通膨將於2026年下半年放緩，明年進一步下降。其基準情境假設中東衝突不會持續增加基礎物價壓力。

這項看法附帶實質條件。Williams表示，如果經濟未沿著使通膨回到2%的路徑發展，採取行動將屬適當；他正關注未來數月的核心通膨數據，是否與2028年前持續達成目標相符。因此，他主張的是有條件的耐心，而非反對緊縮。相較之下，7月的異議官員警告，延後行動可能導致日後必須更積極升息；Williams則更重視能源壓力可望消退。

週一公布的製造業數據使這項預測更加複雜。ISM指數升至55.6，創逾四年最強表現，並明顯高於區分擴張與萎縮的50門檻。報告顯示需求強勁、生產激增，企業也重新增聘人手。ISM調查主席Susan Spence把改善歸因於訂單持續、關稅前景更清晰，以及市場預期戰爭造成的干擾將會減弱。

這波回升之所以重要，在於Williams預期的供給面改善，可能在美國內需依然穩健之際到來。油價下降可壓低整體通膨及部分生產成本，但製造業走強會讓聯準會較難以成長為由，容忍核心通膨持續偏高。即將公布的勞動市場數據因而更加重要，須確認製造業增聘人手究竟代表整體就業仍具韌性，或只是單一產業復甦。

市場定價仍顯示9月升息機率約為70%，10月升息則接近完全反映。這項定價與週一殖利率下降並存，是因為油價回落降低能源衝擊的急迫性，卻未解決政策問題。Williams設定的條件有賴一連串核心通膨數據驗證；異議官員的論點則是，等待本身可能使通膨預期更難控制。

聯準會的溝通問題在較長天期尤其明顯。主席Kevin Warsh表示，較高的債券殖利率已在收緊金融情勢，並刻意減少對未來政策路徑的指引。投資人因而要求更高的通膨與不確定性補償，長端尤為突出。美國銀行利率策略師Mark Cabana把上週賣壓形容為通膨公信力衝擊，並主張聯準會必須說明將如何落實其2%承諾。

Citadel Securities指出，讓市場代替聯準會完成緊縮可能形成循環風險。長期借款成本上升可能促使聯準會等待；但若投資人把等待解讀為決心不足，便可能要求更高的期限與通膨溢價。由升息預期推高的短期利率會更直接抑制需求；若長期利率上升源於政策公信力轉弱，則可能一面增加融資成本，一面削弱通膨框架的可信度。

週一實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步下降，顯示外部通膨衝擊改善時，上述動態可以暫時逆轉。不過，30年期殖利率仍接近上週觸及的5.28%高點，10年期殖利率也仍比一個月前高19.3個基點。單日油價回落減輕了聯準會面臨的壓力，卻未提供投資人認為目前所欠缺的政策反應函數。

## 借款需求增加使供給壓力留在殖利率曲線

美國財政部上調借款預估，使財政供給在週三再融資公告前重新成為焦點。官方目前預計7月至9月一季將借入$7,390億由私人持有的可交易淨債務，比5月預估高$680億。財政部表示，上調主要源於淨現金流下降，季末現金餘額假設則維持在$9,500億。

多數交易商預期，財政部將重申未來至少幾季無須提高票據與債券的標售規模。30年期殖利率已處於2007年以來最高水準，若維持這項指引，便可避免立即增加市場承擔的利率風險供給，也能延續以國庫券滿足較大比例短期融資需求的策略。

由於國庫券利率低於長期債券殖利率，這項策略可降低當前利息支出，卻會增加對前端再融資衝擊的曝險。若聯準會在9月或10月升息，偏重國庫券的債務結構會更快把政策利率上升傳導至財政部借款成本。美國銀行估計，若附息債發行規模到2027財政年度仍保持不變，國庫券占未償債務比重將升至接近25%；若排除全球金融危機及疫情期間的短暫激增，這將是2004年以來最高比重。

市場對新增國庫券仍有可觀需求。貨幣市場基金資產已增至約$8.3兆，穩定幣發行商預料將成為另一項需求來源，聯準會也把部分到期房貸資產回收資金轉投國庫券。這些買方可協助財政部延後增加附息債發行，但無法消除多年來預估接近$2兆赤字所累積的融資需求。

摩根大通分析師估計，若標售規模不變，2027財政年度起將出現資金缺口，至2030年累計短缺達$3.7兆。因此，許多交易商已把預期增加附息債發行的起點延後至2027年5月。少數機構則認為，週三聲明可能弱化現有措辭，讓財政部最早可於2月宣布調整；德意志銀行、富國銀行與CIBC均持此看法。

最終增加哪些券種，與何時增加同樣重要。交易商普遍預期，未來增發將集中在短期與中期附息債，而非10年、20年及30年期券種。財政部5月表示，正研究結構性需求及不同發行配置的成本與風險。若把更多供給配置在曲線前端與中段，可避免對已要求歷史高檔長端溢價的市場再增加過多利率風險。

官方也在考慮是否把財政部剩餘現金投資於附買回市場，並已在再融資前的調查中詢問一級交易商。這類方案可能改變現金餘額波動對短期融資市場的傳導方式，但目前尚未公布任何決定或操作架構。對週一市場而言，差異相當明確：借款預估上調已成事實，標售規模及指引是否調整則仍待決定。

## 捍衛日圓連結官方流動性與美債穩定

日圓在亞洲時段再度大幅升值，引發市場對干預的揣測；其後在紐約交易時段大致穩定於1美元兌157日圓附近。日圓在東京一度上漲1.4%，之後回吐大部分漲幅，美國交易日結束時接近開盤水準。這顯示即使利差仍有利美元，官方可能再次行動的威脅仍可暫時遏止日圓貶值。

日本已證實上週五買進日圓，日本央行帳戶資料顯示，操作規模約為¥5.33兆，折合$340億。前一日的干預估計達¥8.45兆，很可能是東京歷來最大單日操作。日圓此前逼近1美元兌164日圓，創1986年以來最弱水準；連續兩次行動扭轉了逾兩個月的跌勢。

週五金額雖低於週四，卻使本輪行動規模更加清楚。日本央行預估，財政相關因素將使經常帳餘額減少¥11.4兆，降幅大於貨幣經紀商原先預期。日本財務省預定週五公布季度干預報告，但其涵蓋期間為4月至6月，不會提供近期操作完整的逐日明細。

美國的角色不僅限於直接買進日圓。美國財政部長Scott Bessent敦促聯準會提高外國及國際貨幣當局附買回機制（FIMA Repo Facility）的容量。日本表示將使用這項機制，讓外國官方機構能以美債作為擔保換取美元，不必直接出售證券。日本持有逾$1.1兆美債，這條融資管道可避免匯市干預對本已脆弱的美債市場增添直接賣壓。

FIMA目前允許每個交易對手每日最多取得$600億，僅略高於日本估計在週四投入的金額。貸款期限也很短，若干預持續，便須反覆借款或償還。3.75%的操作利率高於一般民間附買回成本，符合其作為流動性後盾、而非永久融資來源的設計。截至7月29日止一週，平均餘額僅$600萬；上次較具規模的使用是2月初的$30億。

這些限制使政策同時具有安撫市場與招致挑戰的效果。FIMA可減少立即出售美債的需要，但若過度強調其容量上限，也可能讓交易員獲得一個可以測試美日承諾的明確門檻。提高單一交易對手上限須獲聯準會外匯小組委員會批准，並讓較廣泛的聯邦公開市場委員會掌握情況。

由於FIMA屬聯準會權限，Bessent公開提出要求本身並不尋常。財政部與聯準會前官員表示，儘管兩個機構都希望限制美債失序賣壓，這類操作討論通常會私下進行。聯準會拒絕置評。這起事件使市場影響之外又多了一項制度問題：華盛頓支持干預日圓，部分是為維護美債穩定，但政府同時也在推動降低國內借款成本。

根本限制仍是利差。日本央行上週把政策利率維持在1%，美國利率區間上限則為3.75%。摩根士丹利、摩根大通、MUFG與ING的策略師認為，如果貨幣政策基本面沒有改變，日圓難以持續升破155太多。週一早盤上漲後回落，也支持這項判斷。政策協調已提高做空日圓的風險，但尚未消除促成這項部位的殖利率優勢。

## 信用融資管道擴大，薄弱結構持續惡化

初級市場顯示，只要殖利率與交易結構足以補償風險，投資人仍願意向體質異常薄弱的借款人提供融資。寮國國營電力生產商EDL-Generation發行$3億、5年期且滿三年可贖回的債券，票息為11.125%。該公司評等落在CCC級，自2000年以來，它是亞洲少數能在非困境債務交換情況下進入美元債市場、評等低於單一B的發行人之一。

募集資金將用於償還9月2日到期的債券及其他債務再融資。EDL-Generation至2027年共有$3.78億債務到期。今年亞洲垃圾債發行額已超過$110億，較2025年同期高約50%，可望成為2021年以來最活躍的一年。這筆交易證明公司仍能取得市場資金，但兩位數票息也顯示，高度投機級借款人延長債務期限所付出的代價。

非洲主權債發行呈現更廣泛的融資管道改善。花旗表示，2026年至今已在當地安排$62億主權融資交易，較去年同期增加約70%，並接近2025年全年承作的$73億。即使中東衝突延續，殖利率下降、美元轉弱及風險偏好仍使肯亞、安哥拉、象牙海岸與加彭等借款人得以籌資。花旗提醒，戰事若持續，可能使下半年發行速度放緩。

阿根廷則選擇不利用同樣開放的市場窗口。經濟部長Luis Caputo重返政府近三年來，未曾發行國際債券，儘管分析師估計海外投資人至少可提供$50億。市場要求的利率約為9%，Caputo認為這與政府推動的財政整頓及經濟改革不相符。

這項選擇維持了降低外部借款成本的目標，卻使阿根廷的準備金緩衝偏薄。民間估計淨準備金接近$100億，而2027年到期的外幣債務超過$250億。政府改在國內發行美元計價債券，取得由世界銀行與美洲開發銀行擔保的$32億銀行貸款，並仰賴農業及Vaca Muerta頁岩區的出口收入。取捨在於：現在避免昂貴發債，或在2027年大選升高政治不確定性之前增加流動性。

中國則提供一項更迫切的再融資考驗。洛陽商都城市投資控股集團原擬發行364天期境外人民幣債券，但因投資人與發行人對定價意見不一而延後。該公司其後表示，已有現金償還8月11日到期、金額人民幣10.8億元的境外債券。這家地方政府融資平台必須償還票息6.9%與7.9%的債券。公司的保證使發債延後尚未演變成已宣布的付款違約，但先前逾期債務與法院強制執行請求，也說明投資人為何要求更高補償。

紐約商業不動產的情況更為嚴峻。一筆以53棟租金穩定公寓大樓為擔保、規模$5.06億的商業不動產抵押貸款證券，其風險最高的券次已累積逾$550萬逾期利息。KBRA Credit Profile估計這些房產價值約為$4.6億，低於債券發行時接近$7.17億的估值，意味債券持有人可能損失逾$8,000萬。債權人上月已加強推動法拍。

A&E Real Estate無法完成再融資，抵押貸款於2024年到期時違約。去年年化支出比原先水準高約22%，收入卻只增加約6%。這批房產每承擔$1債務服務支出，僅產生$0.58收入；服務機構已代墊約$2,900萬，以維持大部分債券利息正常支付。一筆$3,100萬次順位券次的報價約為面額的$0.49，再上一層、規模$4,700萬的券次則約為$0.64。

紐約市長Zohran Mamdani預定10月起凍結約100萬戶公寓租金，可能進一步壓低回收率，因為擔保品中約86%的單位屬租金穩定住宅。Fitch表示，在保險、維修與公用事業成本上升之際，凍租將對估值及再融資構成壓力。Moody’s估計，若凍租長期持續，紐約市CMBS多戶住宅貸款中可能有6%走向潛在違約；不過，由於許多交易也包含市場租金住宅，其判斷整體金融體系的信用風險仍有限。

其他領域的資本市場則持續擴張。今年與野火連結的巨災債券發行額已超過$50億，逼近2025年全年紀錄，反映保險業者把更多氣候風險轉移給投資人。去年整體巨災債券發行量激增45%，推升未償市場規模至$610億。野火模型改善，使單獨承作此類曝險更具可融資性，但歐洲資料的成熟度仍不及加州。

AI基礎設施可能帶來規模大得多的供給變化。Citadel Securities預測，為了替資料中心晶片融資，至2028年公私部門將新增逾$5,000億債務，其中晶片製造商僅在2028年就可能發行逾$2,500億。多數借款預計採3至5年期，以配合晶片生命週期。市場目前已吸收約$5,700億AI相關債務，但預估中的發債潮可能成為投資級信用市場最大的新興產業之一，迫使既有科技業配置騰出空間。

## 前瞻市場意義

週三的美國財政部再融資公告，是長天期債券下一項直接考驗。市場預期附息債標售規模維持不變，但更重要的是，官方是否保留未來至少幾季不會增發的承諾。若措辭允許最快在2月調整，便會使最終增加供給的時點提前；若沿用現有表述，訊號將延後，但本季$7,390億借款需求仍須更多仰賴國庫券滿足。

週五公布的7月就業報告，將檢驗Williams的有條件耐心與7月異議官員偏好提早行動的立場。經濟學家預期非農就業人數增加85,000人，高於6月的57,000人，失業率維持4.2%。若ISM製造業反彈後就業報告仍然強勁，將強化需求足以承受較高利率的論點，也更難以為持續偏高的核心通膨開脫。若數據疲弱，而油價維持在週一較低水準，聯準會便有更大空間等待。

在數據公布前，油價是足以改變政策判斷的變數。若荷莫茲海峽持久重開，通膨補償可望進一步下降，並支持能源衝擊將於下半年消退的看法。若阿曼斡旋管道破裂、美國重新發動攻擊或航運再受干擾，市場便會看清週一美債反彈有多大程度仰賴尚未形成實際協議的談判。

印度央行將於8月5日作出利率決定。由於總裁Sanjay Malhotra認為通膨尚無明顯全面擴散跡象，多數經濟學家預期利率維持不變。吸引海外存款的措施將把美元帶入銀行體系，流動性可能由6月底的5兆盧比增至12月的10兆盧比。這將支撐短天期債券，但全球通膨，以及優惠換匯窗口預定於9月結束，仍會限制長端表現。

日本接下來的考驗，是日圓能否在沒有另一場大規模官方操作下保持穩定。若持續在157附近交易，政策制定者將有時間評估匯市干預與日本央行可能在9月升息能否相互強化。若匯率再度逼近160，則會同時考驗美日兩國所宣示的再次行動意願，以及FIMA在不出售美債的情況下，為反覆干預提供資金的實際能力。

信用市場的判斷重點將不再是融資是否普遍可得，而是體質偏弱的借款人必須接受何種條件。EDL-Generation以11.125%完成再融資，洛陽商都雖延後發債仍表示能夠還款，非洲主權發行也比預期活躍。相反地，紐約公寓證券化案顯示，營運成本上升、浮動利率債務與收入受限若已侵蝕擔保品價值，結果會截然不同。資本市場仍然開放，但資金能否取得，愈來愈取決於價格、結構性保障及可信的還款來源。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有說明，市場水準均以紐約收盤為準。利率資料採Bloomberg每日殖利率歷史序列；變動幅度與衍生曲線均使用相同日期的序列。每日歷史資料未指定觀察時點。

overall_summary.headline: 荷莫茲海峽外交斡旋重啟、油價大跌，帶動美債反彈
overall_summary.session_narrative:
荷莫茲海峽周邊外交斡旋重啟，帶動布蘭特原油下跌6.95%至$83.86、WTI下跌5.14%至$80.32，美債因而沿殖利率曲線全面上漲。2年期殖利率下降5.4個基點至4.238%，5年期下降6.2個基點至4.388%，10年期下降5.8個基點至4.678%，30年期則回落4.5個基點至5.229%。

這波走勢同時反映實質利率與通膨補償下降：10年期實質殖利率下降3.5個基點至2.415%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2.3個基點至2.263%。股市也同步上漲，因為市場把能源成本下降視為通膨及企業利潤率壓力獲得紓解，而非需求崩跌的跡象。

不過，這次漲勢仍只是部分修復。30年期殖利率一週仍上升9.1個基點、一個月上升24.3個基點。Williams支持在核心通膨邁向2028年前持續回到2%的過程中保持耐心，但ISM製造業指數升至55.6，使政策展望仍取決於通膨降溫能否擴及能源以外領域。週三再融資公告前，美國財政部把本季借款預估上調至$7,390億，也形成另一項供給限制。
overall_summary.summary: 荷莫茲海峽外交斡旋重啟，油價下跌並緩解眼前通膨威脅，帶動名目與實質殖利率走低；但核心物價疑慮未退、製造業轉強，加上美國財政部借款需求增加，使長天期債券近期所受損失大致仍未修復。

section_summaries.market_read: 實質殖利率與通膨補償同步下降，顯示這波反彈並非單純由成長疑慮驅動。
section_summaries.summary: 油價下降帶動買盤重返名目美債與抗通膨債券，使殖利率、實質利率與通膨補償同步走低。不過，這波反彈未消除長端近期跌幅；製造業穩健、聯準會耐心附帶條件，以及聯邦借款預估上調，均使市場繼續關注通膨公信力與財政供給。

section_summaries.market_read: 能源風險下降，使長天期債券重新對油價回落產生部分正面反應，但長端仍保留政策、通膨與供給不確定性的溢價。
section_summaries.section_title: 油價回落扭轉當日通膨衝擊
section_summaries.summary: 美國取消原定攻擊，加上重開荷莫茲海峽的磋商取得進展，布蘭特原油下跌近7%、WTI跌逾5%。德黑蘭否認與華盛頓直接談判，原油一個月漲幅仍接近17%，因此市場反映的是近期中斷風險下降，而非和解已完成。中期債殖利率降幅略大於長端，後者的期限溢價仍居高不下。

section_summaries.market_read: 油價回落降低緊縮的急迫性，卻未提供投資人期待聯準會說明的政策反應函數。

section_summaries.summary: Williams表示，目前3.5%至3.75%的目標區間適當，通膨應在2026年下半年放緩；但保持耐心的前提，是核心通膨數據須支持2028年前持續回到2%。ISM製造業指數升至55.6，顯示供給面改善可能與經濟活動穩健並存，使9月政策同時取決於勞動市場韌性及核心通膨是否持續偏高。

section_summaries.market_read: 官方協調提高做空日圓的成本，卻未消除造成日圓弱勢的貨幣政策基本面。

section_summaries.section_title: 捍衛日圓連結官方流動性與美債穩定
section_summaries.summary: 日本確認進場干預後，日圓穩定於1美元兌157日圓附近，其中上週五操作規模約為¥5.33兆。日本計畫使用FIMA附買回機制，可在不直接出售美債的情況下為干預融資；但每日上限、短期限及高於市場的利率限制其作用，美日利差也持續有利美元。

section_summaries.market_read: 只要殖利率、交易結構與還款來源足以補償風險，信用融資仍然可得。
section_summaries.section_title: 信用融資管道擴大，薄弱結構持續惡化
section_summaries.summary: 體質偏弱的借款人仍能取得融資，但條件嚴苛：EDL-Generation以11.125%完成再融資，非洲主權發行加速，阿根廷則拒絕接受接近9%的融資。洛陽商都延後發債，以及紐約公寓證券化案陷入困境，都顯示當定價、擔保品或現金流不足以支撐新債時，再融資風險會迅速升高。
美國財政部再融資指引、7月就業數據，以及荷莫茲海峽外交斡旋能否持續，將檢驗週一長天期債券漲勢是否能夠延續。關鍵在於，能源壓力下降能否先轉化為持續的通膨降溫，抑或經濟活動保持韌性、附息債供給提前，重新推高政策預期與長端殖利率。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied on Aug. 3 as a sharp fall in oil prices reversed part of Friday’s inflation-driven selloff, but the recovery stopped well short of repairing the recent damage to long-duration bonds. The 2-year yield fell 5.4 basis points to 4.238%, the 5-year declined 6.2 basis points to 4.388%, the 10-year dropped 5.8 basis points to 4.678% and the 30-year eased 4.5 basis points to 5.229%. The long bond remained 9.1 basis points higher over the week and 24.3 basis points higher over the month, leaving the market’s concern about Federal Reserve credibility, fiscal borrowing and inflation persistence intact.

Monday’s immediate catalyst was the prospect of renewed diplomacy around the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump called off a planned attack on Iran and said negotiations would seek a full reopening of the waterway, while Iran said separate discussions with Oman on moving more ships were progressing. Brent fell 6.95% to $83.86 and WTI dropped 5.14% to $80.32. The retreat reduced the risk that the energy shock would force an early monetary response and brought buyers back to nominal and inflation-linked Treasuries.

The rally reflected both lower real rates and less inflation compensation. The 10-year real yield fell 3.5 basis points to 2.415%, while the 10-year breakeven declined 2.3 basis points to 2.263%. That combination distinguished the move from a pure growth scare. Equities rose with bonds—the S&P 500 gained 1.48% and the Nasdaq 100 advanced 1.78%—as investors treated cheaper energy as relief for both inflation and corporate margins rather than a warning of collapsing demand.

The day nevertheless supplied reasons for the Fed to remain cautious. The Institute for Supply Management’s manufacturing index rose to 55.6 in July, its highest since May 2022, as demand remained firm, production surged and manufacturers added workers. New York Fed President John Williams said rates were well positioned because he expects inflation to decline during the second half, but he conditioned that patience on core inflation establishing a path consistent with a sustained return to 2% by 2028. The combination of stronger factory activity and lower oil left the September decision dependent on whether disinflation persists beyond energy.

Fiscal financing added a separate restraint on the rally. The Treasury increased its estimate of current-quarter borrowing to $739 billion from $671 billion because projected net cash flows were lower, while retaining a $950 billion end-September cash-balance target. Dealers still largely expected Wednesday’s quarterly refunding to keep coupon auction sizes unchanged, but the larger financing requirement and the growing reliance on bills reinforced the longer-term question of when Treasury must acknowledge the need for more coupon supply.

## Oil Relief Reverses the Daily Inflation Shock

The crude decline was large enough to change Monday’s Treasury direction across the curve. Brent had ended Friday above $90 after gaining more than 20% in July, and the previous session’s rise had lifted both real yields and inflation compensation. By Monday’s New York close, Brent was almost 7% lower and WTI more than 5% lower as the cancellation of planned U.S. strikes reduced the immediate probability of another disruption to Gulf production or shipping.

The diplomatic account was not fully consistent. Trump said talks with Iran were beginning and described reopening Hormuz as the first phase of a broader process that would include the nuclear issue. Tehran denied that it was negotiating directly with Washington, although Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said discussions with Oman about a route through the strait were in their final stages. Israel, which had not joined an earlier June arrangement, was waiting to see whether the initiative produced an enforceable agreement.

That uncertainty kept crude well above its early-July level despite Monday’s drop. WTI remained 16.93% higher over one month and Brent 16.80% higher. The Strait had been repeatedly disrupted during five months of conflict, and a previous U.S.-Iran truce collapsed before another pause was attempted in late July. Monday’s move therefore priced a lower immediate disruption risk, not a completed settlement or a return to the prewar energy regime.

The Treasury curve showed that distinction. The 2s10s spread narrowed only 0.4 basis point to 44 basis points, while the 2s30s spread widened 0.9 basis point to 99.1 basis points. The slightly larger decline in intermediate yields than at the long end reflected relief around policy and inflation without eliminating the term premium embedded in a 30-year yield still above 5.2%. Over the previous week, 2s30s had steepened 17.6 basis points.

Long-duration performance likewise remained a partial recovery. The ICE U.S. Government 20-plus-year index gained 0.39% on Monday but was still down 1.46% over the week and 3.56% over one month. The 7-to-10-year index rose 0.23% on the day and remained 1.04% lower over a month. Monday restored some price sensitivity to falling energy costs, but it did not reverse the cumulative increase in the real discount rate or the premium attached to long-run policy and supply uncertainty.

Treasury trading activity was much lighter than at Friday’s month-end adjustment. FINRA recorded $1.106 trillion of par activity, down 42.4% from the prior session, across 379,162 trades. Nominal-coupon activity fell 43.7% to $854.6 billion, while TIPS activity declined 71.4% to $34.7 billion. Turnover in coupons longer than 7 years through 10 years fell 48.8% to $142.9 billion. The reduced activity does not identify investor direction, but it shows that the rally occurred with substantially less repositioning than Friday’s selloff.

Risk assets confirmed that lower oil was the dominant cross-market impulse. The S&P 500 closed at 7,600.50, within reach of a record, while the Nasdaq 100 gained more than the broader market. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 1.05%, although it remained down 9.47% over one month. The VIX edged down to 15.86. Gold futures rose 1.45% to $4,107.80 even as the immediate energy risk receded, while the dollar index gained 0.22% after having lost 1.47% over the preceding week.

## Williams Defines the Conditions for Fed Patience

Williams supplied a more patient policy signal than the three officials who dissented in favor of a rate increase at the July meeting. He said the existing 3.5%-to-3.75% target range was well positioned to support disinflation and forecast that inflation would ease during the second half of 2026 and decline further next year. His base case assumed that the Middle East conflict would not keep adding to underlying price pressure.

The qualification was substantive. Williams said action would be appropriate if the economy was not following a path that returned inflation to 2%, and he was concentrating on whether core readings over the next several months were consistent with reaching the target sustainably by 2028. His position was therefore conditional patience rather than an objection to tightening. It placed more weight on the expected fading of energy pressure than the July dissenters, who warned that delay could require more aggressive increases later.

Monday’s manufacturing release complicated that forecast. The ISM index rose to 55.6, the strongest reading in more than four years and clearly above the 50 threshold separating expansion from contraction. The report described strong demand, a surge in production and renewed hiring. ISM survey chair Susan Spence attributed the improvement to sustained orders, greater clarity around tariffs and expectations that war-related disruptions would diminish.

The rebound was important because it indicated that the supply-side relief anticipated by Williams could arrive while domestic activity remained firm. Lower oil would reduce headline inflation and some production costs, but manufacturing strength would give the Fed less reason to tolerate persistent core inflation on growth grounds. The result also raised the importance of the coming labor data, which must show whether factory hiring reflects broader employment resilience or a sector-specific recovery.

Market pricing still assigned roughly a 70% probability to a September increase, with an October move close to fully priced. That probability coexisted with Monday’s yield decline because oil reduced the urgency of the energy shock without resolving the policy question. Williams’s threshold depends on a sequence of core inflation readings, while the dissenters’ case rests on the risk that waiting itself allows expectations to become harder to contain.

The communication problem is most visible at longer maturities. Chair Kevin Warsh has said higher bond yields are already tightening financial conditions and has deliberately reduced guidance about the likely policy path. Investors have responded by demanding greater compensation for inflation and uncertainty, especially in the long end. Bank of America rates strategist Mark Cabana characterized last week’s selloff as an inflation-credibility shock and argued that the Fed needs to explain how its commitment to 2% will be implemented.

Citadel Securities identified a circular risk in allowing markets to perform the tightening. Higher long-term borrowing costs can persuade the Fed to wait, but if investors interpret that wait as insufficient commitment, they may demand still greater term and inflation premiums. Short rates driven higher by expectations of Fed action restrain demand more directly; long rates rising because policy credibility has weakened can impose financing costs while making the inflation framework less secure.

Monday’s lower real yield and breakeven showed that this dynamic can temporarily reverse when the external inflation impulse improves. Yet the 30-year yield remained close to the 5.28% peak reached last week, and the 10-year was still 19.3 basis points above its level one month earlier. A single day of oil relief reduced the pressure on the Fed; it did not supply the reaction function investors said was missing.

## Larger Borrowing Needs Keep Supply in the Curve

The Treasury’s revised borrowing estimate brought fiscal supply back into focus before Wednesday’s refunding announcement. Officials now expect to borrow $739 billion in privately held net marketable debt during the July-to-September quarter, $68 billion more than projected in May. The department attributed the increase mainly to lower net cash flows and kept its end-quarter cash-balance assumption at $950 billion.

Most dealers expected Treasury to repeat that note and bond auction sizes need not rise for at least the next several quarters. Retaining that guidance would avoid an immediate increase in duration supply when the 30-year yield is already at its highest since 2007. It would also preserve the strategy of using bills to meet a larger share of near-term financing needs.

That strategy reduces current interest expense because bill rates are below long-term yields, but it increases exposure to front-end refinancing shocks. If the Fed raises rates in September or October, a bill-heavy structure passes higher policy rates into Treasury’s borrowing costs more quickly. Bank of America estimated that keeping coupon issuance stable through fiscal 2027 would lift bills to nearly 25% of outstanding debt, excluding the temporary surges during the global financial crisis and pandemic. That would be the highest share since 2004 on that basis.

Demand for additional bills remains substantial. Money-market fund assets have grown to about $8.3 trillion, stablecoin issuers are expected to add another source of demand, and the Fed is recycling maturing mortgage holdings partly into bills. Those buyers can help Treasury defer coupon increases, but they do not remove the cumulative funding requirement created by deficits expected to run near $2 trillion for years.

JPMorgan analysts estimate that unchanged auction sizes would begin leaving a funding gap in fiscal 2027 and produce a cumulative $3.7 trillion shortfall through 2030. Many dealers have consequently moved their expected start for coupon increases to May 2027. A minority, including Deutsche Bank, Wells Fargo and CIBC, saw a possibility that Wednesday’s statement would soften the existing language enough to allow an announcement as early as February.

The eventual composition matters as much as the timing. Dealers generally expect future increases to be concentrated in short- and intermediate-term coupons rather than the 10-, 20- and 30-year sectors. Treasury said in May that it was studying structural demand and the costs and risks of different issuance profiles. Directing more supply toward the front and belly would limit the additional duration placed into a market already charging a historically high long-end premium.

Officials are also considering whether surplus Treasury cash could be invested in the repo market, after asking primary dealers about the idea in the pre-refunding survey. Such a program could alter the transmission of cash-balance swings through short-term funding, although no decision or operating framework has been announced. For Monday’s market, the immediate distinction was simpler: the borrowing estimate was realized news, while auction sizes and any change in guidance remained pending decisions.

## Yen Defense Links Official Liquidity to Treasury Stability

The yen stabilized near 157 per dollar through the New York session after another sharp Asian-hours advance revived speculation about intervention. It had gained as much as 1.4% in Tokyo before surrendering most of the move. The currency finished the U.S. day near where it began, suggesting that the threat of renewed official action could arrest depreciation temporarily even though the interest-rate differential continued to favor the dollar.

Japan confirmed that it bought yen on Friday, and Bank of Japan account data indicated an operation of about ¥5.33 trillion, or $34 billion. That followed an estimated ¥8.45 trillion intervention the previous day, likely the largest single-day operation by Tokyo. The two actions reversed more than two months of yen losses after the currency had approached 164 per dollar, its weakest level since 1986.

The Friday amount was smaller than Thursday’s but brought the scale of the campaign into clearer view. The BOJ projection showed an ¥11.4 trillion fiscal-related decline in the current-account balance when money brokers had expected a smaller change. Japan’s Finance Ministry is due to publish a quarterly intervention report on Friday, although its April-to-June coverage will not provide the complete daily breakdown for the latest operations.

The U.S. role extends beyond direct purchases of yen. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent encouraged the Fed to increase the capacity of its Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility. Japan said it would use the facility, which permits foreign official institutions to pledge Treasuries for dollars instead of selling the securities outright. Because Japan owns more than $1.1 trillion of Treasuries, the funding route can prevent currency defense from adding outright selling pressure to an already-fragile U.S. bond market.

The facility currently permits as much as $60 billion per counterparty per day. That is only modestly more than Japan was estimated to have spent on Thursday, and the loans are short term, requiring repeated borrowing or repayment if intervention continues. The 3.75% offering rate is also above ordinary private repo costs, consistent with its design as a liquidity backstop rather than a permanent funding source. Balances averaged just $6 million in the week through July 29, and the last significant use was $3 billion in early February.

Those limits create a tension between reassurance and challenge. FIMA reduces the need for immediate Treasury sales, but emphasizing a capped facility may give traders a measurable point against which to test the U.S.-Japan commitment. An increase in the counterparty limit would require approval from the Fed’s foreign-currency subcommittee, with the broader Federal Open Market Committee kept informed.

Bessent’s public request was itself unusual because the facility sits under Fed authority. Former Treasury and Fed officials said such operational discussions would typically occur privately, even though both institutions share an interest in limiting disorderly Treasury sales. The Fed declined to comment. The episode adds an institutional question to the market impact: Washington is supporting yen intervention partly to protect Treasury stability while the administration is also pressing for lower domestic borrowing costs.

The fundamental constraint remains the rate gap. The BOJ kept its policy rate at 1% last week, compared with the 3.75% upper bound of the U.S. range, and strategists at Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, MUFG and ING saw little scope for a sustained yen advance much beyond 155 without a change in monetary fundamentals. Monday’s retreat from an early gain supported that assessment. Coordination has increased the risk of betting against the yen, but it has not yet removed the yield advantage that encouraged the position.

## Credit Access Expands While Weak Structures Deteriorate

Primary markets showed that investors remained willing to finance unusually weak borrowers when yield and structure were sufficient. EDL-Generation, a state-owned Laotian power producer, sold $300 million of 5-year notes callable after three years with an 11.125% coupon. Rated in the triple-C tier, it was one of only a handful of Asian issuers below single-B to access the dollar market outside a distressed exchange since 2000.

The proceeds will repay a note due Sept. 2 and refinance other obligations. EDL-Generation has $378 million of debt maturing through 2027. The sale occurred as Asian junk-bond issuance exceeded $11 billion for the year, about 50% above the comparable 2025 period and on course for the busiest year since 2021. The transaction demonstrated access, but the double-digit coupon showed the cost of extending maturities for a deeply speculative borrower.

African sovereign issuance presented a broader version of that access. Citigroup said it had arranged $6.2 billion of sovereign transactions in the region during 2026, about 70% more than at the same point last year and approaching the $7.3 billion it handled in all of 2025. Lower yields, a weaker dollar and risk appetite had allowed borrowers including Kenya, Angola, Ivory Coast and Gabon to raise funds despite the Middle East conflict. Citi cautioned that continued fighting could slow issuance during the second half.

Argentina was choosing not to use a similarly open window. Economy Minister Luis Caputo had sold no international bond during nearly three years back in government, even though analysts estimated foreign investors could provide at least $5 billion. The market was demanding roughly 9%, a rate Caputo considered inconsistent with the government’s fiscal consolidation and economic reforms.

The choice preserves the objective of lowering external borrowing costs but leaves Argentina with a thin reserve cushion. Private estimates put net reserves near $10 billion, while more than $25 billion of foreign-currency debt falls due in 2027. The government has instead issued dollar-denominated bonds domestically, secured $3.2 billion of bank loans backed by the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank, and relied on export receipts from agriculture and the Vaca Muerta shale formation. The trade-off is between avoiding expensive debt today and adding liquidity before the 2027 election increases political uncertainty.

China supplied a nearer-term refinancing test. Luoyang Shangdu City Investment Holding Group said it had cash to repay 1.08 billion yuan of offshore notes due Aug. 11 after postponing a planned 364-day offshore yuan bond because investors and the issuer disagreed over pricing. The local-government financing vehicle must repay 6.9% and 7.9% notes. Its assurance prevented the delayed sale from becoming an announced payment failure, but earlier overdue obligations and a court-enforcement claim showed why investors demanded more compensation.

The contrast was sharper in New York commercial real estate. A $506 million commercial mortgage-backed security backed by 53 rent-stabilized apartment buildings has accumulated more than $5.5 million of past-due interest on its riskiest tranches. KBRA Credit Profile values the properties at about $460 million, down from an appraisal near $717 million when the bonds were issued, implying more than $80 million of bondholder losses. Creditors escalated foreclosure efforts last month.

The mortgage defaulted at its 2024 maturity after A&E Real Estate could not refinance. Annualized expenses were about 22% above original levels last year, while revenue was only about 6% higher. The properties generated 58 cents for each dollar of debt service, and the servicer has advanced about $29 million to keep most bond interest current. A $31 million junior tranche was quoted near 49 cents on the dollar and the next $47 million slice near 64 cents.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s rent freeze, scheduled to begin in October for about 1 million apartments, threatens to reduce recoveries further because roughly 86% of the collateral units are rent stabilized. Fitch said the freeze would pressure valuations and refinancing as insurance, maintenance and utility costs rise. Moody’s estimated that a prolonged freeze could push 6% of New York City’s CMBS multifamily loans toward potential default, while judging systemwide credit risk limited partly because many deals also contain market-rate units.

Capital markets were expanding in other areas. Wildfire-linked catastrophe-bond issuance exceeded $5 billion during the year, approaching the record for all of 2025, as insurers transferred more climate risk to investors. Overall catastrophe-bond issuance had surged 45% last year, lifting the outstanding market to $61 billion. Better wildfire models are making standalone exposure more financeable, although European data remain less mature than California’s.

AI infrastructure could bring a much larger supply shift. Citadel Securities forecast more than $500 billion of additional public and private debt by 2028 to finance chips for data centers, with more than $250 billion potentially issued by chipmakers in 2028 alone. Much of the borrowing is expected in 3-to-5-year maturities to match chip life cycles. Markets have already absorbed roughly $570 billion of AI-related debt, but the projected wave could become one of the largest new sectors in investment-grade credit and force existing technology allocations to make room for it.

## Forward Market Significance

Wednesday’s Treasury refunding announcement is the next direct test for duration. The market expects coupon auction sizes to remain unchanged, but the more important question is whether officials preserve the promise of no increases for at least several quarters. Language allowing an adjustment as early as February would bring the eventual supply increase closer; retaining the existing formulation would defer the signal while leaving the $739 billion current-quarter borrowing need to be met more heavily through bills.

The July employment report on Friday will test Williams’s conditional patience against the July dissenters’ preference for earlier action. Economists expect payrolls to rise by 85,000 after June’s 57,000 gain, with unemployment holding at 4.2%. A strong report following the ISM manufacturing rebound would strengthen the case that demand can withstand higher rates and make persistent core inflation harder to excuse. A weak result would give the Fed more room to wait if oil remains near Monday’s lower level.

Oil is the variable capable of changing that policy assessment before the data arrive. A durable reopening of Hormuz would extend the decline in inflation compensation and support the view that the energy shock will fade during the second half. A breakdown in the Oman channel, renewed U.S. strikes or another shipping disruption would expose how much of Monday’s Treasury rally depended on negotiations that had not yet produced an implemented agreement.

The Reserve Bank of India decides on Aug. 5. Most economists expect it to keep rates unchanged as Governor Sanjay Malhotra sees little evidence that inflation is becoming broad-based. Liquidity could rise toward 10 trillion rupees by December from 5 trillion at the end of June as measures attracting overseas deposits bring dollars into the banking system. That supports shorter-dated bonds, while global inflation and the scheduled end of the concessional swap window in September constrain the long end.

Japan’s next test is whether the yen can remain stable without another large official operation. Sustained trading near 157 would give policymakers time to assess whether intervention and a possible September BOJ increase can reinforce each other. A renewed approach toward 160 would test both the declared willingness of the U.S. and Japan to act again and the practical capacity of FIMA to finance repeated intervention without Treasury sales.

Credit will be judged less by broad availability than by the terms attached to weak borrowers. EDL-Generation secured refinancing at 11.125%, Luoyang Shangdu says it can repay despite postponing its sale, and African sovereigns have issued more actively than expected. The New York apartment securitization shows the opposite outcome when higher operating costs, floating-rate debt and constrained revenues have already eroded collateral value. Those cases leave capital open, but increasingly conditional on price, structural protection and a credible source of repayment.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally as renewed Hormuz diplomacy drives oil sharply lower
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied across the curve as renewed diplomacy around the Strait of Hormuz drove Brent down 6.95% to $83.86 and WTI down 5.14% to $80.32. The 2-year yield fell 5.4 basis points to 4.238%, the 5-year declined 6.2 basis points to 4.388%, the 10-year dropped 5.8 basis points to 4.678% and the 30-year eased 4.5 basis points to 5.229%.

The move reflected both lower real rates and less inflation compensation: the 10-year real yield fell 3.5 basis points to 2.415%, while the 10-year breakeven declined 2.3 basis points to 2.263%. Equities also advanced as cheaper energy was treated as relief for inflation and corporate margins rather than evidence of collapsing demand.

The rally remained a partial recovery. The 30-year yield was still 9.1 basis points higher over the week and 24.3 basis points higher over the month. Williams supported patience while core inflation moves toward a sustained return to 2% by 2028, but the ISM manufacturing index’s rise to 55.6 kept the policy outlook dependent on whether disinflation extends beyond energy. Treasury’s increase in projected current-quarter borrowing to $739 billion added a separate supply constraint before Wednesday’s refunding announcement.
overall_summary.summary: Falling oil prices pulled nominal and real yields lower as renewed Hormuz diplomacy eased the immediate inflation threat, but persistent core-price concerns, stronger manufacturing and larger Treasury borrowing needs left the recent damage to long-duration bonds largely intact.
